content:
Noah: Heads-up: AE asking for exception on a 2-year prepaid deal with Fjord Media. Ask: 40% off if they prepay 24 months up front. They claim strategic content partnership and high likelihood to expand. Need finance + accounting + tax + RevMgr approval.

Sofia: 40% is huge. Policy: discounts >=30% require RevManager + Finance Director + Accounting sign-off. Also prepaid revenue recognition and deferred rev treatment must be validated.

Ava: Quick numbers: ```
List 24mo list price: $240,000
40% prepaid price: $144,000 (delta = -$96,000)
Immediate cash today: +$144k vs normal monthly collections
Accounting impact: $144k deferred revenue to recognize over 24 months; potential cash vs revenue mismatch and ASC 606 considerations.
```

Marcus: Sales argues early cash helps Q and partner channel opens 10x pipeline. They want a short approval fast. Propose guardrails: discount applies only to specified SKU, non-transferable, no additional promos, and an expansion price floor for year 3. Also propose a $50k maximum aggregate concession (but that conflicts with numbers).

AccountingBot: Policy check: prepaid deals with >1-year term and material discounts require Accounting Director involvement. Need revenue recognition memo, amortization schedule, and cap table impact. Please attach deal-desk form and revenue model. Internal docs: https://intranet.redwood/accounting/prepaid-policy (internal).

TaxOps: Flag: large prepays can create nexus and VAT/WHT exposure depending on customer country. Need customer tax ID and country billing entity. If funds are paid upfront, may create withholding or VAT obligations. Please provide customer tax residency and invoicing plan.

Sofia: Risk assessment: Biggest risks are (1) precedent for deep discounts, (2) revenue-recognition complexity, (3) tax withholdings in customer's jurisdiction, (4) cash impact if customer churns and requests refund. Suggest non-refundable clause for a portion (e.g., 25%) and a 12-month minimum commitment with clawback if they downgrade before 12 months.

Ava: Revised guardrails proposed by Sales: 35% max discount instead of 40%, 24mo prepay allowed only with a 50% non-refundable deposit, cap total concession at $60k, require Exec sponsor, and require TaxOps sign-off on invoicing. If we keep 40% we must escalate to CFO.

Noah: @RevManager can you review? We need decision today to keep the customer engaged. I've attached the deal summary in CRM (link internal).

RevManager: I can review but 40% is outside my comfort band. Will approve 35% with the guardrails Ava listed: 50% non-refundable deposit, $60k concession cap, Accounting memo and amort schedule, and TaxOps clearance. If Sales insists on 40% they must get CFO sign-off and provide Exec sponsor note.

TaxOps: Also require customer tax cert and invoice to be routed to our AP team for VAT handling. If they are in EMEA we may need to register for local VAT or apply VAT reverse charge. We'll confirm after we get customer tax details.

AccountingBot: Once deal-desk form + revenue model + invoice plan uploaded, I will route to Accounting Director and generate required deferred revenue entries. Marking thread: deal-desk:pending.

Noah: Sales to update CRM with requested guardrails and upload docs by 2623456900. If all checks pass we'll route for final sign-off. :thumbsup:
